Question 3
?

The electrical resistivity of a copper wire varies with the temperature. The function R(T) gives the resistivity of a wire at a temperature of T degrees Celsius. What is the best interpretation of R′(10)=−0.01?

a
At 10 degrees Celsius, the resistivity of the wire increases at a rate of 0.01 units per degree
b
For each interval of 10 degrees Celsius, the resistivity of the wire decreases by 0.01 units
c
At 10 degrees Celsius, the resistivity of the wire is 0.01 units
d
At 10 degrees Celsius, the resistivity of the wire is 0.01 units less than its value at 0∘
e
At 10 degrees Celsius, the resistivity of the wire decreases at a rate of 0.01 units per degree
